name: Logistics & Supply Chain Management
focus: Supply chain strategy and design, sourcing and procurement, supplier relationships, inventory and distribution, transport and warehousing, risk and resilience, sustainability.
theories: Fisher's supply chain matrix (functional vs innovative products)
The bullwhip effect (Lee, Padmanabhan and Whang)
Lean, agile and leagile supply chains (Christopher; Naylor)
Total cost of ownership and total landed cost
Economic order quantity and safety stock
Supply chain risk management and resilience (Christopher and Peck)

name: Operations Management
focus: Process design, capacity and bottlenecks, quality management, lean and just-in-time, planning and control, service operations, productivity, technology and automation in operations.
theories: Slack's five performance objectives (quality, speed, dependability, flexibility, cost)
The four Vs of operations (volume, variety, variation, visibility)
Lean and the Toyota Production System, the seven wastes (Ohno)
Total quality management and the PDCA cycle (Deming)
The Hayes and Wheelwright four-stage model
Capacity strategies (lead, lag, match) and trade-off theory (Skinner)
The SERVQUAL gap model (Parasuraman, Zeithaml and Berry)

name: Strategic Planning
focus: Competitive advantage, industry and environment analysis, resources and capabilities, growth and diversification, mergers and alliances, business models, strategy implementation.

name: People, Work & Organisations
focus: Motivation and job design, organisational culture and structure, groups and teams, human resource management, employment relations, organisational change, diversity, wellbeing, the future of work.
theories: The Job Characteristics Model (Hackman and Oldham)
Scientific management (Taylor) and the human relations school (Mayo)
Tuckman's stages of group development and Belbin's team roles
Lewin's three-step change model and force field analysis
Hard and soft HRM (the Michigan and Harvard models)

name: Leadership
focus: Leadership theories, power and influence, ethics and responsibility, decision making, leading change, developing leaders, followership.
theories: The Blake and Mouton managerial grid
French and Raven's bases of power

name: Economics for Business
focus: Demand, supply and pricing, costs and market structures, competition and regulation, macroeconomic conditions, international trade, exchange rates, labour markets.
theories: Market structures (perfect competition, monopoly, oligopoly, monopolistic competition)
Monetary and fiscal policy and the business cycle

name: Financial Decision Making
focus: Financial statements and ratios, working capital and cash flow, investment appraisal, cost of capital, capital structure, budgeting, risk management, valuation.
theories: Net present value, internal rate of return and payback
The weighted average cost of capital and CAPM
Capital structure theory (Modigliani and Miller, trade-off, pecking order)
Working capital management and the cash conversion cycle
Ratio analysis and the DuPont model
Risk and return and portfolio theory (Markowitz)

name: Strategic Marketing
focus: Segmentation, targeting and positioning, brands, the marketing mix, pricing, customer experience and loyalty, consumer behaviour, digital marketing, market research.
theories: Customer-based brand equity (Keller) and Aaker's brand equity model
Relationship marketing and customer lifetime value

name: Delivering Successful Projects
focus: Project life cycle, scope, time and cost, planning and scheduling, risk and stakeholder management, governance, agile and waterfall methods, benefits realisation, why projects fail.
theories: The project life cycle and stage gates
Work breakdown structure, critical path method and PERT
Project risk management and the risk register
The planning fallacy and reference class forecasting (Kahneman; Flyvbjerg)
